decisions.reason: It directly builds on the firm's core knowledge in authentication, encryption and trusted second-channel communication, so absorptive capacity for improving and commercializing it is high.
A mobile PDF signature function fits the firm's move toward app-based interactions and online contract signing and leverages its existing identity and cryptography capabilities.
A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is very close to the firm's established security stack and R&D base, making it a strong candidate for continued refinement rather than withdrawal.

Secure email-to-app delivery is adjacent to the firm's secure communication and mobile-channel expertise, though it is somewhat more niche and therefore faces a modestly higher risk of being streamlined.

While related to the firm's cryptography and hardware experience, a QR-code-based hardware signature token is less aligned with its strategic shift toward integrated, app-centric identity solutions and is more likely to be deprioritized.

A payment network security compliance suite matches the firm's strength in regulated, high-risk digital interactions, even if its vertical focus makes it somewhat less central than the core identity products.
